message: Kotlin writes $title into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).
Kotlin writes $title into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it.

Kotlin writes $target at the start of href, so the value decides the scheme, and a javascript: URL runs. Escaping does not help: start the value with /, # or https://, or build the string with interpolate(...), which refuses a scheme that runs.
Kotlin writes $code into a script or style element, which the browser runs, so escaping does not help. Put the value in a data-* attribute or a signal and read it from there.
Kotlin writes $code into onclick, which the browser runs, so escaping does not help. Put the value in a data-* attribute or a signal and read it from there.

Kotlin writes $query into data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Text from outside becomes code there, even inside quotes. Put the value in a signal, or in an attribute of its own read with el.dataset; only a number or a boolean is safe to write in.
Kotlin writes $width into an attribute value without quotes, where a space starts a new attribute. Quote the value.
Kotlin writes $count here, a number from the server, which is safe in a Datastar expression. Meant as the signal $count, make the literal $$"""...""" (Kotlin 2.2+), or escape as ${'$'}count.

Kotlin writes the value `name` into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).
Unknown action @GET. Did you mean @get?
Unknown modifier __debunce on data-on, which Datastar ignores, so it listens for the event click. Did you mean __debounce?
Unknown Datastar attribute data-onn. Did you mean data-on?
Datastar expression: Unexpected token
This is an aliased Datastar attribute, but the prefix is set to data-. Check streamlord.attributePrefix.
The CSP nonce is empty. Datastar raises NonceRequired for an empty data-nonce and does not start.
Datastar reads $my-count as one signal named my-count, and nothing here declares it: a key my-count is the signal $myCount. For a subtraction write $my - count, with spaces.
No markup or code in the project defines the signal 'nobodyInTheForgeDefinesThis'.
data-text does not take a key.
data-bind needs a signal, as a key or as a value; without one Datastar raises KeyOrValueRequired.
Kotlin fills in $query before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the value to interpolate.
interpolate throws IllegalArgumentException here: the markup has 2 %s placeholders and 1 value is given. Write %% for a per cent sign that is not a placeholder.

interpolate always throws here: code lands in a script or style element, which the browser runs, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Put the value in a data-* attribute or a signal and read it from there; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

interpolate always throws here: code lands in onclick, which the browser runs, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Put the value in a data-* attribute or a signal and read it from there; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).
